content.title: UConn vs. Michigan NCAA championship game odds, injury report, prediction
content.text: April 4, 2026Updated April 6, 2026, 12:32 a.m. ETWhat do the oddsmakers and injury reports say about the men's basketball NCAA championship game - UConn vs. Michigan?Let's look at which team is the favorite, the odds, injuries, when the game takes place and share a prediction about which team will advance.When is UConn vs. Michigan? How to watchMonday, April 6No. 2 UConn vs. No. 1 Michigan| 8:50 p.m. ET | TBS | Sling TVMarch Madness Elite 8 odds for UConn vs. MichiganPrices below were current at time of publication as listed by Draftkings Sportsbook.What is the point spread for UConn vs. MichiganMichigan is the favorite at -7.5What is the over/under for UConn vs. Michigan144.5What is the moneyline for UConn vs. MichiganMichigan is -298, UConn is +240Injury report for UConn vs. MichiganUConn guard Solo Ball is back from a wrist injury to full strength or pretty close to it - he had 13 points on 5-for-11 shooting against Illinois. After a quiet first half, he scored 10 points in the second half, including key shots and a fastbreak dunk that helped the Huskies maintain their lead. Ball with heavy taping on the wrist against Duke went 0-for-5 from deep and 3-for-11 from the field.No more worries either on Michigan guard Elliot Cadeau who fell ill from an allergic reaction to something he ate early in the week. He looked just fine against Arizona.There were additional concerns raised about Michigan's Yaxel Lendeborg and UConn's Ball from Saturday's action but both were left off their team's respective NCAA initial player availability reports that were released at 9 p.m. ET on Sunday.Prediction for UConn vs. MichiganMichigan beat UConn 59-0 the last time they met - in football. Thankfully for Huskies' fans, UConn has a 2-1 edge in men's basketball. The last hoops' meeting was a 74-60 Huskies' victory on November 25, 2015. This is the first time the programs will meet in the NCAA Tournament. The pick here is Michigan because No. 1 seeds are due - the No. 1s have failed to win the tournament the last three years (a long drought, considering No. 1s have won 65% of the tournaments since 1985).
